subject: Dedicated capacity integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + autoscaling sizing
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Harris <tom.harris@polarishealth.com>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@polarishealth.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + autoscaling sizing

Thanks for the call today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move the Dedicated evaluation forward.

Recap / asks (short):
- SDK & auth: you asked about SDK setup, SSO, and long-lived API keys for backend jobs. We support API keys + optional SAML + customer-managed KMS. Can you confirm whether your integration team needs SAML-only or API-key for server-to-server?
- Routing: you mentioned wanting region-based routing + fallback to hosted model variants. We'll recommend a primary us-west region with automatic fallback to us-east for capacity. Any constraints on cross-region data movement?
- Structured output / tool calling: we demoed function/tool calling. We should capture the top 3 actions you expect the model to perform (e.g., extract structured case metadata, call diagnostics service, populate EHR fields).
- Embeddings / rerankers: you plan to index ~5k clinical docs and run reranking for retrieval-augmented generation. Estimate: ~5k vectors initially, indexed monthly. Confirm expected QPS for embedding updates vs. query QPS.
- Autoscaling & throughput sizing (Dedicated): you asked how Dedicated can be sized — please confirm target steady-state and peak QPS, and percent of requests that require low-latency (<200ms) vs. best-effort. Also list concurrent session expectations.

Attachments: I attached a draft SOW and the auth/routing diagram we sketched on the call.

Proposed next steps:
1) You provide: steady-state QPS, expected burst QPS, average token lengths for generation and embedding batch sizes.
2) Our infra team (Logan) will propose a Dedicated capacity configuration: reserved GPU pool size, concurrency limits per model, queue sizing and autoscaling thresholds.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical review next week with your infra lead + our runtime eng. Is Wed 3/24 10:00am PT good?

Thanks — looping in Logan and Aditya for sizing and architecture notes.

-- 
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity integration follow-up: SDK/auth/routing + autoscaling sizing

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A few answers from our side below.

Performance & traffic:
- Steady-state: ~200 requests/sec (these are mostly short prompts, ~120 tokens on average).
- Peak bursts: up to ~600 rps for 10-15 minute windows during batch processing and clinician shifts.
- Low-latency requirement: ~60% of requests need sub-200ms 99th pct; the rest can be relaxed.
- Concurrent sessions: approx 350 concurrent user sessions at peak (many short-lived).

Embeddings & reranking:
- Initial corpus: ~5,000 clinical notes; we plan monthly adds of ~1,000 documents.
- Query QPS for retrieval: ~120 qps with reranker calls per top-10 results.
- Embedding update jobs can be scheduled off-peak; we expect 2 large batch jobs per day.

Auth / SDK:
- We prefer SAML SSO for interactive console access and API keys for server-to-server calls (long-lived keys rotated monthly).
- SDK: our platform team will use the Python SDK; please share sample auth flow and how to inject customer API keys in the Dedicated deployment.

Routing & data residency:
- All PHI must remain in us-west primary region; cross-region fallback is allowed only for non-PHI traffic. We can mark requests that contain PHI to avoid cross-region fallback.

Queue behavior / session affinity:
- We have some long-running sessions that pin state (KV caches). Can you confirm behavior for session affinity and KV cache eviction when autoscaling scales the pool down?

I attached a short network constraints doc and our security contact if you need anything for compliance review.

If Wed 3/24 10am PT works for you, we'll confirm and include our infra lead.

Thanks,
Tom
Director, Platform Engineering, Polaris Health
tharris@polarishealth.com

Attachment: polaris-network-constraints.pdf (pdf, 620KB)

- steady 200 rps, bursts to 600 rps; 60% sub-200ms 99th pct; ~350 concurrent sessions; embedding query QPS ~120 with reranker.
- PHI must stay in us-west; cross-region fallback only for non-PHI. They will mark PHI requests.

- A short ops playbook for how restarts/scale-downs affect active sessions and how we recommend using sticky routing or pool pinning for PHI workloads.

Quick priority: preserve low-latency for 60% of traffic and ensure PHI workloads never leave us-west.

--
Marissa

Tom — thanks for the details and the doc. Quick reply with the proposed plan from our side so you have something concrete before the tech call: 

Proposed Dedicated config (initial):
- Reserved pool: 8 A100-style GPU equivalents (reserved) with ability to burst +4 GPUs for up to 30 minutes.
- Autoscaling: scale-up when queued requests > 25% of pool capacity for 2 consecutive minutes; scale-down after sustained underutilization for 10 minutes.
- Concurrency limits: cap concurrent decoding requests per GPU to 40 (we'll pick per-model limits in the tech call), with request-level concurrency isolation for reranker jobs.
- Queue sizing: soft queue max 4,000 requests (global) with per-customer sub-queue of 1,000 and per-model queue TTL 120s. Requests beyond that trigger graceful fallback to hosted models for non-PHI traffic.
- KV cache / session affinity: recommend sticky routing for PHI sessions (pin to a reserved subset of the pool) to preserve KV cache; evictions on scale-down will prefer non-PA (non-PHI) sessions. We'll document expected cache TTL and eviction policy in the ops playbook.

SDK / Auth notes:
- We'll share a Python SDK snippet for server-to-server usage showing API key injection and key rotation guidance.
- For SAML console access we'll provide steps to configure SSO and map roles.

Next steps:
1) Logan / Aditya: can you refine GPU type, exact concurrency-per-GPU numbers by Monday EOD so I can send a formal recommendation to Tom?
2) Tom: confirm Wed 3/24 10:00am PT for the technical review and I'll send a calendar invite with a short agenda.
3) I'll circulate a one-page ops playbook + sample SDK snippet ahead of the call.

If this looks good I'll convert to a short proposal and attach an updated SOW link (DocuSign once agreed).

Thanks,
Marissa
